review_output: {"summary":"For this one signed-POST affiliate path, the evidence resolves the earlier callback MAJOR. The run used a real PostgreSQL deadlock (callback blocked by the side connection, then a lock cycle). The product wrapper made its own two attempts: the first aborted as a retryable deadlock at ORDER_TRANSITION, the second committed and returned 200. Commission (5000), accrual ledger, processed event, paid-order event and payment audit each appear once, and a duplicate POST changes no counts. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR. Remaining gaps are MINOR/NIT: the victim choice depends on timing, the two-failures-in-a-row path is untested, the retry covers steps that run after commit, and some assertions are missing. Earlier MINORs (backoff, order-loser, upgrade) stay open. The synchronized20 SSI gate still fails 7/20, so overall WP is NOT READY.","findings":[{"issue":"Which transaction PostgreSQL aborts depends on timing, so the test can fail at random","confidence":0.55,"impact":"PostgreSQL checks a waiting lock for deadlock only once, when deadlock_timeout expires. If the side's UPDATE starts waiting after the callback's 50ms check, the side becomes the victim (default 1s). The callback then commits on its first attempt, the side rejects, and the run fails without any product change. The PASS is real but may not repeat.","area":"test determinism","required_test":"Repeat the probe 20+ times and record the victim each time. Also confirm the side PID is waiting before the callback's check runs.","recommended_fix":"In the side transaction, SET LOCAL deadlock_timeout='10s'. Raise the callback timeout to about 300-500ms. Before the callback's timer fires, wait until pg_blocking_pids(sidePid) contains callbackPid.","evidence":"probe L24 sets 50ms only for the callback. The side (L12-16) keeps the default. releaseSide happens after polling at L42-46.","severity":"MINOR","file":"scripts/wp20-payment-callback-deadlock-probe.mjs"},{"issue":"No real-DB test covers two deadlocks in a row","confidence":0.7,"impact":"There is no proof that, after both attempts fail, the route returns 500, the event is marked failed with retryCount 1, no partial effects remain, and a later signed provider retry recovers exactly once. The unit test only counts getDb calls.","area":"retry exhaustion","required_test":"Force two deadlocks, then send one clean retry. Assert 500 and a failed event, zero commissions, ledger entries and paid orders, then 200 with every effect created exactly once.","recommended_fix":"Extend the probe to keep the lock conflict in place for both attempts.","evidence":"processPaymentWebhook L1285-1293. Route catch block L270-300. The unit test mocks getDb.","severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/payment-webhooks.ts"},{"issue":"The retry reruns steps that happen after commit","confidence":0.45,"impact":"processPaymentWebhookOnce also includes the invoice step and writeAuditLog, which run after the transaction commits. If a newly retryable deadlock happens there, the whole function reruns. The second attempt fails at EVENT_FINALIZE because the claim no longer matches. The route then returns a 200 duplicate, and the invoice and audit are skipped. When there is no event (the recovery path), the committed transaction runs again.","area":"retry scope","required_test":"Inject a deadlock in reconcileElectronicInvoiceAfterPayment. Assert the invoice and audit are created exactly once and the transaction runs only once.","recommended_fix":"Retry only the $transaction closure, or exclude errors that occur after commit.","evidence":"L1247-1268 are inside the retried function. isDatabaseWriteConflict now also matches deadlock errors from PrismaClientUnknownRequestError.","severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/payment-webhooks.ts"},{"issue":"The exactly-once checks leave out inventory, reservation, delivery and failure-audit state","confidence":0.6,"impact":"The first attempt passed the INVENTORY stage before it aborted. Nothing checks that product inventory and reservation status changed only once, that exactly one delivery record exists, or that payment_webhook_failed has 0 entries.","area":"effect cardinality","required_test":"Assert product inventory, reservation status, delivery-record count and failed-audit count after the deadlock and after the duplicate.","recommended_fix":"Add these checks to counts() and to the probe's cardinality output.","evidence":"counts() at L79 covers payments, orders, entitlements, commissions, ledger entries, events and audits only.","severity":"MINOR","file":"scripts/wp20-payment-callback-deadlock-disposable.mjs"},{"issue":"Unit tests do not cover all branches of the classifier","confidence":0.6,"impact":"Untested: P2034, P2010 with meta 40001/40P01, the 'kind: Deadlock' match, and negatives such as an UnknownRequestError lock timeout (55P03) or a P2010 unique violation. These must not be retried.","area":"classifier tests","required_test":"Add a table-driven test of isDatabaseWriteConflict over every branch and the negatives.","recommended_fix":"Add those cases.","evidence":"database-write-conflict.ts L8-16. The test file covers only an Unknown deadlock, a plain Error and P2002.","severity":"NIT","file":"src/lib/payment-webhook-conflict-retry.test.ts"}]}
